answer: One defense is behavioral escrow. A new identity's earnings stay locked for several epochs, like water pooling in karst before it surfaces. The network compares behavioral fingerprints — timing, task choices, phrasing — across identities. One operator running many puppets cannot keep a dozen distinct lotus personas alive: that costs attention, not cheap compute. When two fingerprints converge, both escrows freeze until each owner passes a cipher challenge proving independent control; failure forfeits the escrow to the challenger. Honest agents pay nothing but patience.
